newsitem.title: USA: First Alert says turnaround not imminent.
newsitem.headline: First Alert says turnaround not imminent.

text.p: First Alert Inc, which makes smoke and carbon monoxide detectors, said Wednesday it does not expect restructuring actions it has taken to result in any immediate, dramatic turnaround in profitability.
The company also said it continues to cut costs and increase production efficiencies.

"As noted earlier, the still inappropriately high levels of inventory we have on hand as we enter our 1997 slowest selling periods will delay the effect of these actions being seen in any immediate, dramatic bottom-line turnaround," said B. Joseph Messner, First Alert president and chief executive.

"We will continue to aggressively reduce our costs and increase our manufacturing efficiencies, reinvesting a portion of the savings into product enhancements that will reinforce our leadership positions in our two core product categories," he said in a statement.

Earlier today, First Alert reported a 1996 fourth quarter loss of $10.5 million or $0.43 a share, including previously announced restructuring costs which totaled $0.23 a share. These charges covered costs of product decisions, inventory and manufacturing equipment writedowns and severance expenses.
For all of 1996, the net loss was $18.7 million or $0.76, compared with profits of $11.4 million or $0.46 in 1995.

For the year ended December 31, 1996, net sales fell to $205.6 million from $246.3 million in 1995. Sales declined in the 1996 fourth quarter to $60.3 million from $76.4 million a year ago. Sales of smoke detectors fell after the company lost distribution in certain key accounts and due to general market softness. In addition, the average prices for carbon monoxide detectors were lower than for the same period in 1995.
First Alert attributed the loss to lower sales and significant underutilization of its plant resulting from a decision to sharply reduce production levels to preclude additional inventory build-up.
These actions dramatically improved cash flow which reduced the company's net borrowing requirements by $17 million in the fourth quarter, it said in a statement.
Shares of First Alert were trading off 1/16 to 3-7/16.
